items.title: 12.9 The asymmetry of matter and antimatter in the universe

source_refs.note: Topic 12.9 (PDF 274, printed 271). The hydrogen and helium percentages differ from those given in 12.10 (68% and 27%); recorded.

blocks.text: Many observations show that there is an asymmetry between matter and antimatter; this is one of the most remarkable features of our universe. A number of observations indicate that the universe consists almost entirely of matter rather than antimatter. For example, the universe is assumed to have about 5% ordinary matter (electrons, protons and neutrons), with this matter about 72% hydrogen and 24% helium, and there is no contribution of antihydrogen or antihelium atoms to the composition of the universe.

The matter-antimatter asymmetry is due to the violation of conservation of baryon number, that is, an imbalance between the number of baryons and antibaryons. If particle-antiparticle symmetry is also violated, there would be a mechanism for making more quarks than antiquarks, more leptons than antileptons, and eventually more matter than antimatter. Hence it is concluded that the asymmetry of matter and antimatter is still a mystery.
